record.paper_title:
AIM Workshop “Pólya-Schur-Lax Problems: Hyperbolicity and Stability
Preservers” — A List of Open Problems
record.context_brief: Positivity of Taylor coefficients after logarithm
record.original_question:
Suppose f ∈ R[z1, z2] is real stable, satisfies f(0,0)=1, and has only
nonnegative Taylor coefficients. Must the
function (z1, z2) ↦ -log(f(-z1,-z2)) also have only nonnegative Taylor
coefficients?

evidence.quote: Problem 40 ([14, 15]). Suppose that f ∈ R[z1 , z2 ] is real stable with f (0, 0) = 1 and that all Taylor coefficients of f are non-negative.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f \in \mathbb{R}[z_1, z_2]$ be a real stable polynomial in two variables, i.e., $f$ has real coefficients and $f(z_1, z_2) \neq 0$ whenever both $z_1$ and $z_2$ lie in the open upper half plane $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Im}(z) > 0\}$. Assume in addition that $f(0,0) = 1$ and that every Taylor coefficient of $f$ at the origin is nonnegative. Define
\[
g(z_1, z_2) \;=\; -\log f(-z_1, -z_2),
\]
viewed as a formal power series at the origin (well-defined since $f(0,0)=1$). Must every Taylor coefficient of $g$ at the origin be nonnegative?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in the AIM workshop problem list on Pólya–Schur–Lax problems, attributed to work of Borcea–Brändén (and collaborators). A web search returned no published resolution; surveys on stable polynomials discuss related positivity/log-concavity properties but no proof or counterexample for this two-variable statement was found.
